scenes.narration: The popular story is that everything declines sharply after thirty. Most of that is marketing, not physiology.
Cardiovascular capacity falls about five to ten percent a decade in people who never train it. Trained adults lose closer to one percent.
Muscle and bone respond to load at any age. Older beginners still gain strength rapidly when they start.
What really changes is recovery, which takes longer, and that is easy to misread as lost ability.
The body does not switch off at thirty. It starts demanding that you be deliberate instead of coasting, and deliberate is a strategy anyone can learn.
Two or three resistance sessions a week, most weeks, plus walking. Boring, unglamorous, and the only approach that has ever survived the evidence.
